Team / Sarah —

As we prep for Stratus's QBR (renewal due mid-December) I want a tight pack for execs that surfaces the renewal risk matrix and three ask-level items requiring leadership attention. I've attached an initial risk matrix (redwood_renewal_risk_matrix_v1.xlsx) — it's rough but maps product, reliability, and pricing risks against impact/time-to-fix.

Quick asks:
- Jordan: consolidate a one-slide customer-health summary (usage, latency, error spikes, top support cases). Keep it short — 3 bullets + 1 chart.
- Grace: pull the 90/30/7-day usage and latency trends and note any billing anomalies (token spikes).
- Markus: summary of the sept/oct incident (root cause, mitigations in prod, ETA for full fix) — one-paragraph plus timeline.
- Sarah / Procurements: confirm renewal posture (intent to renew, any procurement steps required) and if Stratus has any outstanding compliance evidence requests ahead of renewal.

I want to iterate quickly: please reply with your inputs by Tuesday EOD PST so we can create the exec one-pager and MAP (mutual action plan) to share with the Stratus execs on Wed.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi

Irene / team — posting the incident timeline and the high-level RCA pointer below.

Incident: Oct 29, 2026 — intermittent model latency regressions on long-sequence requests affecting 3% of production traffic.
Root cause (summary): a regression in the attention caching path caused KV cache evictions under specific sequence-length distributions. A model runtime micro-optimization introduced a cache invalidation edge case under high variation workloads.
Mitigation to date:
- Oct 30: rollback micro-optimization to safe kernel path (reduced latency by ~40% for affected requests)
- Oct 31: applied temporary autoscaling policy for long-sequence workers
Planned full fix:
- Nov 10: deploy patched caching logic with additional unit/integration tests
- Nov 17: monitor for 2 weeks and validate drop in incident rate to <0.5%
Exec ask (3 sentences): This issue exposed a kernel-level caching fragility that increases latency risk for long-sequence workloads. We request an expedited engineering priority to land the patched caching logic (ETA Nov 10) and a temporary capacity buffer to avoid customer impact during rollout. Failure to prioritize increases renewal risk for customers with heavy long-sequence usage.

Attachment: incident-timeline.txt

Markus Klein
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
